A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZoomEye. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original ZoomEye experiments on V*Bench, HR-Bench, and MME-RealWorld, including robustness tests and case analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds evaluations with newer models and analyses of search steps, zoom success, and image partitioning.

M1.justification: Section 3 and v1 Appendix A/v2 Appendix D retain cue generation, the four-way image tree, confidence-based ranking, stopping rules, input strategies, and final patch aggregation. Additional backbones and partitioning ablations do not establish a revised core algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate V*Bench, HR-Bench 4K/8K, and the same MME-RealWorld monitoring, driving, OCR, and remote-sensing tasks. Diagram/table tasks remain excluded. The new experiments use this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds VisCrop and Pixel Reasoner to the comparisons while retaining V* and DC2. It removes the DC2/LLaVA-v1.5-13B comparison and InternVL-1.5-26B baseline row. Tables 2 and 8 also introduce Qwen2.5VL and InternVL2.5 baselines paired with ZoomEye.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5VL-3B and InternVL2.5-4B/8B/26B configurations. Section 4.4 introduces threshold variation, accuracy conditioned on at least 50% target-object coverage, and comparisons of 4/9/16 sub-regions with average search steps. The earlier AnyRes-block sweep is removed; retained benchmark settings are otherwise largely unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's AnyRes-block sensitivity study in Section 4.5 and Figure 4 is removed. v2 Section 4.4 adds search-step scaling, successful-versus-failed zoom analysis, and partitioning-granularity ablations. Existing qualitative examples and orientation/position error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained algorithmic confidence scores do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds model, comparator, and ablation results in Tables 2, 4–6, and 8; older LLaVA and MME-RealWorld scores are retained. The reported DC2/LLaVA-v1.5-7B V* score changes from 57.3 to 57.60. AnyRes curves and DC2/13B results disappear. Some added gain figures are inconsistent: v2 reports a 14.19-point LLaVA-ov-7B V* gain, although its retained scores, 75.39 and 90.58, imply 15.19 points.

T1.justification: The formal tree-search representation, autoregressive formulation, image-input equation, confidence calculations, weighting function, and appendix algorithms remain substantively unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 makes vision-level test-time scaling an explicit contribution and conclusion claim, replacing v1's contribution emphasis on AnyRes robustness. It retains training-free, model-agnostic zooming but drops the earlier first-effort novelty claim and broadens the highlighted model results.

C2.justification: v2 Section 6 adds substantive limitations concerning heuristic search, fragmented cues from fixed partitions, and document-layout tasks. Section 4.4 adds interpretations about search-effort tradeoffs, zoom success, and partitioning robustness; Appendix B explains advantages over single-crop and trained approaches. The earlier orientation and global/local position limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 Section 4.1 specifies settings for added models, including Qwen2.5VL's 12,845,056-pixel cap and InternVL's 12-block cap. Existing prompts, threshold schedules, patch-pasting details, and pseudocode move from Appendix A to D without substantive changes. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions ZoomEye around visual reasoning and test-time scaling, citing o1, DeepSeek-R1, and newer multimodal reasoning work and contrasting its open approach with o3. Appendix B adds substantive positioning against VisCrop and Pixel Reasoner. The first-effort claim and older citations such as Visual Sketchpad and Dragonfly are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around vision-level reasoning and scaling. Experiments are reorganized into ablations and comparison subsections, DC2 discussion moves to an appendix, and the appendices are reordered into A–D. Dedicated limitations and acknowledgements sections appear, and citations change to author–year style.

P2.justification: High-resolution results are reorganized across v2 Tables 2 and 8 with shaded gain rows. New analysis tables appear, the DC2 comparison becomes a broader table, and the two-panel AnyRes plot is replaced by a search-step curve. Existing illustrations, prompt boxes, and algorithms are largely retained but reflowed within a different page format.

improvement.justification: The added Qwen2.5VL and InternVL2.5 experiments strengthen model-agnostic evidence beyond v1's LLaVA-family tests, while new analyses and explicit limitations improve scrutiny of the method. These gains are tempered by removal of the AnyRes robustness study and new numerical inconsistencies: the abstract claims InternVL2.5-8B HR gains of 15.71% and 17.69%, whereas Table 2 supports 9.13 and 16.25 percentage points.
